presentation.title: Small models for your custom harness needs
presentation.body: Start with the real labels and transcript text you already exported from Transcript Lake. The trainer validates and retains that corpus, then fits one small local classifier per aspect; no synthetic starter labels are created.

presentation.title: Adopt an existing labeled corpus
presentation.body: Choose a schema-v1 dataset-bundle JSON previously written by this trainer's Transcript Lake/Stado export boundary. Every record is validated before the content-addressed immutable copy and selection registry are changed. Unknown fields, malformed timestamps, empty text, and duplicate native session IDs reject the whole bundle. Re-adopting identical content is unchanged; older corpora remain retained. You may skip and keep an empty usable trainer.

presentation.title: The lake is read, and never written
presentation.body: An adopted bundle is a read-only snapshot under the trainer's own training root. Without one, ground truth is read live through the transcript-lake CLI. In both cases the trainer never writes Transcript Lake labels. Model artifacts and metrics remain outside the lake.

presentation.title: Train one aspect from the labels you already made
presentation.body: One classifier per aspect, TF-IDF and logistic regression by default, trains locally. It needs enough real labeled sessions over at least two values; the trainer never pads the corpus with sample rows. This step is satisfied only once a trained artifact exists under the training root.

presentation.title: Read the first labels the small model suggests
presentation.body: Inference prints label-store-shaped records only after the classifier evaluates real transcript text. Those suggestions are the first successful product result and remain yours to review; applying one is still the Transcript Lake labeler's job.
